summary: The note explains how local political parties shape education policy, using the Evergreen Education Alliance (EEA) in the City of Evergreen as a running example. It walks through a seven-step reform process, from identifying issues to feedback and adjustment, with dated examples. It stresses community engagement and notes that local policies can serve as pilots for wider regional or national reform.
one_line: Local parties like Evergreen's EEA drive education reform through a seven-step process of identification, proposal, advocacy, legislation, implementation, evaluation and feedback.
key_facts: The Evergreen Education Alliance (EEA) began a mission on September 5, 2023 to revise educational frameworks for the 21st-century learner.
On October 14, 2023, the City Council, with a majority of EEA members, passed a resolution to increase technology grants for public schools.
On October 29, 2023, Council Member Helen Ramirez of the Evergreen School Reform Committee (a branch of the EEA) said discussions with teachers showed a need for reduced class sizes.
The EEA took two months, from November 2023 to January 2024, to draft a policy on integrating environmental science into the elementary curriculum.
On January 15, 2024, the EEA organized a city-wide education summit at Evergreen High School that showed strong public support.
On February 20, 2024, the EEA passed a motion to introduce a pilot after-school program for academic support and career readiness.
In March 2024, the Evergreen School District began rolling out the after-school program, with monitoring by EEA members.
In April 2024, the EEA partnered with Evergreen State University for a six-month assessment of the after-school program's impact on student performance and engagement.
On May 30, 2024, public forums were set up for Evergreen residents to voice observations and concerns about current education policies.

The reform process has seven steps: identifying the issue, developing a proposal, advocating for adoption, navigating legislative procedures, implementation, monitoring and evaluation, and feedback and policy adjustment.
The EEA's success is attributed to consistent outreach and a bottom-up approach involving students, parents, educators and local experts.
The EEA's tech grant increase is being reviewed for potential state-wide expansion as of June 2023.
